hint.text: Commas can be used to clarify meaning in a sentence. This can help avoid ambiguity or misinterpretation.

instruction.text: Match each <t-blue>blue sentence</t-blue> to the text that has the same meaning.

atoms.a: <t-blue>Sam loves painting his dogs and old films.</t-blue>
atoms.b: Sam loves to paint pictures of his dogs. Sam also loves to paint pictures of old films.

atoms.a: <t-blue>Sam loves painting, his dogs and old films.</t-blue>
atoms.b: Sam loves to paint. Sam also loves his dogs. Sam also loves old films.

instruction.text: Match each <t-blue>blue sentence</t-blue> to the text that has the same meaning.

atoms.a: <t-blue>The child asked, “Are we going to draw Mr Smith?”</t-blue>
atoms.b: The child asked if we are going to draw pictures of Mr Smith.

atoms.a: <t-blue>The child asked, “Are we going to draw, Mr Smith?”</t-blue>
atoms.b: The child asked Mr Smith if we are going to draw pictures.

instruction.text: Match each <t-blue>blue sentence</t-blue> to the text that has the same meaning.

atoms.a: <t-blue>Milly loves cooking her sisters and her friends.</t-blue>
atoms.b: Watch out! Milly loves cooking her sisters. Milly also loves cooking her friends.

atoms.a: <t-blue>Milly loves cooking, her sisters and her friends.</t-blue>
atoms.b: Milly loves to cook. Milly also loves her sisters. Milly also loves her friends.

instruction.text: Add commas to make the meaning of the sentence clearer.

atoms.sound: To Sam, Mira, Henry and Clara all seemed lovely.
atoms.b: To Sam((,)) Mira((,)) Henry and Clara all seemed lovely.

atoms.sound: While the family cooked, the dogs played in the garden.
atoms.b: While the family cooked((,))the dogs played in the garden.
